newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: SIMEX Brent crude trades higher on technicals.
newsitem.headline: SIMEX Brent crude trades higher on technicals.

text.p: SIMEX Brent crude traded higher late afternoon on Tuesday on firm technicals which brokers said are showing the start of a bullish trend.

They said the market had initially ridden on the back of nervous trading after Iraq decided to proceed with its plans to send helicopters to pick up Moslem pilgrims from the Saudi border despite U.S. warning.
But one broker said the effect of this news was tapering off as the market largely discounted possible action by the United Nations which could threaten the oil-for-food-deal with Iraq.
June last traded at $18.42 per barrel, up eight cents from its previous close in London, while July last traded at $18.51, also up eight cents.
Traders said after breaking the initial resistance of $18.35, the next resistance for June Brent is seen at $18.50 and $18.75.
NYMEX on the after-hours ACCESS system last traded at $20.08 for June, up one cent from its official close on Monday.
